LGTM. To me it beats having to remember to rm /var/configuration/system.json every time.
LGTM

A little more description here would be good.  The goal of the cache is not to "avoid re parsing" it's to handle "new devices detected" on firmware updates.  Should we reword this in terms of the user facing feature, rather than what the code does internally?  (Ie, support new-device detection).

FWIW, I suspect if worded that way, and modified slightly, there's a lot of users that would opt for this mode.

Changed it to also mention the interaction with the new-device detection feature.

I left the stuff about configuration parsing in there since i consider editing configuration something a user might do.

And re-parsing the configuration is a side effect of setting the option to false, which is a behavior that's visible to the user (their changes will be applied on EM restart).

> FWIW, I suspect if worded that way, and modified slightly, there's a lot of users that would opt for this mode.

Nice to hear that!

Can we name the option "new-device detection" please?  The description is great, but I'd like the build-facing feature to be tied to external behavior, not internal specifics.

The fact that EM uses a file to accomplish new device detection that isn't important to the feature itself, and might change over time.  The platform.json was originally meant for a use case that no longer exists, reactors reading the "platform config" from the filesystem.  That's all moved to dbus a long time ago, so ultimately this was never really a "cache", just a way to know how to change system states.
Done

This will now issue "new device found" events on every boot, which is the whole intent of this file existing.  Fine if you want to remove it, but you should add a check in the new device logic to not log that event if this option is enabled, because all devices will be "new" devices.
Done. Had not thought about the interactions with that feature, thanks for pointing it out 👍
can we avoid duplicating this check in two places?  Just put this conditional on line 1317 once, and avoid this whole block if it's not enabled.
Done.
Please structure your option like this.  Set the define if it's enabled.
Done
I don't think your code will compile when set to false as it is now, as this global var won't be defined.  You would need to use an #ifdef or have it write a something to a config.h.

Can we use #if instead?

Why use the preprocessor if we do not have to?

Using conditional compilation excludes some of the code from parsing and typechecking.

Since only one configuration of meson options is compiled in CI,
this increases the likelihood of permutations of these options 
which then do not compile.


There is almost never a need to actually use the preprocessor if you have a modern compiler which can do const value propagation and dead code elimination.


It's also better for LSP and code navigation to not use the preprocessor.
An LSP aware code editor may not be able to navigate code that is not 'compiled'.
